title: image_picker
objectives: Understand image_picker via a real-life analogy
Pick from camera or gallery — single + multi + video
Handle iOS PHPickerViewController + Android Photo Picker (scoped storage)
Fall back gracefully on desktop / web / emulator

sections.markdown:
**Think of `image_picker` as the 'system attach photo' dialog you see in every messenger app.**

User taps 'Attach.' The OS shows its native picker — gallery + camera + files sometimes — and returns the chosen file(s). You get a path (or bytes on Web). That's it. No preview, no in-app UI to design.

- **Simple** — 3 lines of code for a picker; fits 80 % of 'upload a photo' needs.
- **Native UX** — the user's brain already knows the flow; no learning curve.
- **Modern pickers** — iOS 14+ uses `PHPickerViewController` (no photo library permission needed for pick-only flows); Android 13+ uses Android Photo Picker (scoped access without READ_MEDIA_IMAGES permission).
- **Not for guided capture** — if you need overlays, barcode reads, real-time preview, use the `camera` plugin.
- **Compression + resize** — built-in `maxWidth / maxHeight / imageQuality` params handle it before returning the file.

**Why every consumer Flutter app uses it for profile-picture / attach-photo flows:** the OS already ships an excellent picker; matching it in-app is 100× more work for no user benefit. Users trust the system UI. Also — with iOS PHPicker + Android Photo Picker, you don't even need the photo-library permission for a pick-only flow, dramatically reducing permission-prompt friction.

**`image_picker`** wraps the OS photo picker: `PHPickerViewController` (iOS 14+), Android Photo Picker (Android 13+, backport via `androidx.activity.result.PickVisualMedia`), file dialogs on desktop/Web. Two source flavors: `ImageSource.camera` (opens native camera app) or `ImageSource.gallery`. Returns `XFile` (single) or `List<XFile>` (multi). Compression: `maxWidth`, `maxHeight`, `imageQuality`. Also picks videos: `pickVideo()`.

sections.markdown: ## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Requesting photo-library permission on iOS 14+ for pick-only flows.** PHPicker doesn't need it. If you request unnecessarily, users get an extra prompt they may deny.
**Mistake 2: Ignoring `PlatformException`.** User denies camera permission → PlatformException. Catch + show explainer.

**Mistake 3: Uploading full-resolution.** A modern phone shoots 12 MP = ~5 MB JPEG. Compress via `maxWidth: 1600` + `imageQuality: 85` before upload — usually enough for any web UI, saves bandwidth 10-20×.
**Mistake 4: Missing lost-data recovery on Android.** If the OS kills your app during the pick (low memory), `retrieveLostData` recovers the selected file on next launch. Skip = silent data loss.
**Mistake 5: Assuming `path` is stable.** iOS returns a temp path; may be deleted after the app terminates. Copy to app documents if you need to keep.
**Mistake 6: EXIF leaks GPS.** Photos taken with camera have GPS coordinates in EXIF. `requestFullMetadata: false` strips it; also possible to strip via the `image` package.
**Mistake 7: Not handling `null` return.** User cancels the picker → returns null. Guard.
**Mistake 8: Web bytes vs mobile path.** On Web, `XFile.path` is a blob URL, not a real path — use `await file.readAsBytes()` for upload.
## Best practices
**1. Prefer PHPicker / Android Photo Picker** — no permission for pick-only.
**2. Compress before upload** — `maxWidth: 1600 + imageQuality: 85` is a solid default.
**3. Strip EXIF GPS** via `requestFullMetadata: false` OR the `image` package.
**4. Copy to persistent path** if you need to keep beyond the current session.
**5. Recover Android lost data** via `retrieveLostData` on app launch.
**6. Handle `PlatformException` + null cancels gracefully.**
**7. `XFile.readAsBytes` on Web** for upload.
**8. Fall back to `file_picker`** for generic file selection when you don't want images-only.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Pick single from gallery + preview.
**Practice 2 (Easy)** — Camera snap + display + save.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Multi-pick + horizontal ListView preview.
**Practice 4 (Medium)** — Compress via `maxWidth + imageQuality`; report file-size delta.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — Android low-memory kill recovery via `retrieveLostData`.
**Practice 6 (Hard)** — Strip EXIF GPS + upload via Dio multipart.
**Practice 7 (Expert)** — Fallback flow: image_picker fails → `camera` plugin flow → file_picker last-resort.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: When would you pick `image_picker` over `camera` plugin?**

**A:** `image_picker` — one-off 'attach a photo' flows: profile picture, chat attachment, KYC ID upload where system camera works. The OS provides the whole UI; you get one file back. **Advantages:** minimal code (5 lines), native permissions handling, users know the UX. `camera` plugin — need overlay UI (barcode scanner, guided document capture, KYC face capture with detection ring), real-time preview manipulation, image-stream to ML Kit, custom controls (zoom, exposure). **Cost:** much more code + lifecycle care. **Rule:** if the answer to 'do I need custom UI over the preview?' is 'no', use `image_picker`. **Modern bonus:** iOS PHPicker + Android Photo Picker require no photo-library permission for pick-only flows — using image_picker actually reduces prompts vs rolling your own.

**Q2: What changed with PHPickerViewController (iOS 14+) and Android Photo Picker?**

**A:** **PHPickerViewController** (iOS 14+, replaces `UIImagePickerController` for gallery): the system runs the picker **out-of-process**, returns copies of the selected images to your app. Your app **never sees the full photo library** — no permission needed. Reduces prompt friction + is required for App Store approval for pick-only flows going forward. **Android Photo Picker** (Android 13+; back-port via `androidx.activity.result.PickVisualMedia` down to Android 4.4): equivalent system picker. `image_picker` uses these automatically. **Implication:** the old advice ('need `Photos` permission to pick') is obsolete for the pick-only case. If you need to READ full library, iterate all photos, or do EXIF/live-photo work — that still needs the permission. **Interviewer bonus:** knowing 'permission-less pick' is a specific answer that separates junior from senior candidates.

**Q3: How do you compress + resize before upload?**

**A:** `pickImage(maxWidth: 1600, maxHeight: 1600, imageQuality: 85)` — the plugin re-encodes as JPEG at 85% quality after resizing to fit within 1600 px. **Why 1600 + 85?** — max reasonable UI display size on modern screens is ~2 K; 85 % JPEG is visually lossless at that size; typical output is 200-500 KB (vs 5 MB original). **When you need custom control:** use the `image` or `flutter_image_compress` package after picking — supports PNG, WebP, EXIF stripping, aspect ratio preservation. **Video:** limited built-in compression; use `video_compress` for aggressive re-encoding. **Server-side re-compression** — always do it at the server too; users may bypass client compression. **Anti-pattern:** upload full 12 MP; cellular users will drop off + your bill will explode.

**Q4: What's `retrieveLostData` and when do you call it?**

**A:** **Android-only.** If your app is killed by the OS while the picker is open (rare but real on low-memory devices), your `pickImage` future never resolves. On next launch, `picker.retrieveLostData()` returns the file the user had selected. **Where to call:** in `main`, after Firebase init, before showing the UI. **Handle:** if `lost.file != null`, resume the intended flow (upload / show preview); if `lost.exception != null`, log + show error. **Not needed on iOS** — the system re-launches into the picker. Overlooking this = users complaining 'I picked a photo, went away for 30 s, came back, nothing happened' — silent data loss.

**Q5: Web + desktop targets — what to know?**

**A:** **Web:** `image_picker` uses a `<input type="file">` element. `XFile.path` is a blob URL — NOT a real file path. To upload, `await file.readAsBytes()` and send bytes. **No `ImageSource.camera` support** on all browsers (requires `getUserMedia`). **Desktop (Windows/macOS/Linux):** file dialog picker. `pickImage(ImageSource.camera)` on desktop opens a webcam via CameraX-equivalents on some platforms — mostly missing. Fallback: use `file_picker` (better desktop story) or open the platform-native camera app externally. **Trap:** running on desktop in dev without a webcam — plugin errors. Feature-detect + gracefully degrade. **Common pattern:** `if (kIsWeb || !Platform.isMobile) → show file_picker; else → image_picker`.

**Q6: Privacy — what should you strip / not track?**

**A:** **(1) EXIF GPS** — photos have latitude/longitude embedded. `requestFullMetadata: false` strips before returning. Alternatively `image` package after pick. **(2) Timestamps** — creation date leaks user timezone; not usually a concern but consider for anonymized flows. **(3) Face detection metadata** — some devices embed facial data in EXIF; strip for anonymous flows. **(4) Cross-user upload** — same photo uploaded by 2 users can reveal shared context; server-side hash + dedup carefully. **(5) Consent for uploads** — 'we'll upload this to our servers, delete anytime' — required under GDPR / DPDPA. **(6) Server-side scanning** — many apps scan uploaded images for CSAM / illegal content; part of Trust & Safety, but disclose in ToS. **(7) Don't request full library** access when pick-only will do — respects user privacy + reduces attack surface.

## Real-world usage

- **Chat / messenger apps** — attach photo/video.
- **Profile / KYC** — avatar upload, ID card capture.
- **Product listings** — sellers upload catalog images.
- **Reviews** — attach a review photo.
- **NOT ideal for** — guided capture (use `camera`); general file picking (use `file_picker`).

## Advanced notes

- **`pickMedia`** — new combined images + videos picker (iOS 14+, Android modern).
- **`XFile.readAsBytes`** — cross-platform bytes access.
- **`preferredCameraDevice: CameraDevice.front`** — hint the front camera on iOS (Android varies).
- **`imageQuality: 100`** — no compression; may return larger than source for some formats.
- **`maxDuration` for video** — truncated to fit.
- **EXIF stripping** via `image` package: `decodeJpg` → `encodeJpg` re-encodes without EXIF.
- **File extension handling** — HEIC/HEIF on iOS may need conversion via `flutter_image_compress` for backend compatibility.
- **UploadedXFile lifecycle** — copy to persistent path if needed later.
- **`file_picker` alternative** — better desktop + multi-file support.
- **Video thumbnails** — separate package `video_thumbnail`.
- **iOS 17+ 'limited access' library** — user grants access to a subset; PHPicker sidesteps this by design.
- **Testing** — mock `ImagePickerPlatform` via `flutter_test`'s method-channel overrides.
